name: Shephatiah (Ancestor of Meshullam, from the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chron. 9:8))
title: Benjaminite ancestor
summary: Shephatiah is a person mentioned in 1 Chronicles 9:8 as an ancestor of Meshullam, from the tribe of Benjamin. He is noted in connection with the list of Israelites who settled in Jerusalem after returning from exile in Babylon. His significance lies in his role in the genealogy that links the tribe of Benjamin to the rebuilding of Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the Genealogy of Benjamin
keyEvents.description: Shephatiah is mentioned as the son of Reuel and an ancestor of Meshullam in the list of Benjaminites who settled in Jerusalem after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Repopulation of Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: The genealogy in 1 Chronicles 9 describes how Israelites from various tribes, including Shephatiah's descendants from Benjamin, returned to settle in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

keyEvents.title: Presence of the Tribe of Benjamin in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Shephatiah's lineage is part of the broader list of Benjaminites who helped restore the population of Jerusalem, highlighting the tribe's continued significance.

keyEvents.title: Parallel to Nehemiah's list
keyEvents.description: The book of Nehemiah contains a corresponding list of Jerusalem's inhabitants after the exile, confirming the importance of documenting genealogies for those who returned.
